s:
Consider the following statements about the Tejas Light Combat Aircraft:
1. It was designed by the Aeronautical Development Agency (ADA) and is built by HAL.
2. It was named by Atal Bihari Vajpayee.
3. The Tejas Mk-2 is to be powered by the Rolls-Royce Adour engine.
4. It is India's first indigenous fly-by-wire aircraft.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct: Tejas was designed by ADA, built by HAL, named by Vajpayee, and is India's first indigenous fly-by-wire aircraft. Statement 3 is wrong: the Mk-2 (with canards) is to be powered by the GE F414 engine.

s:
Match List-I (Platform) with List-II (Role):
List-I | List-II
a. Dhruv | i. Light combat helicopter for high altitude
b. LCH Prachand | ii. Light trainer aircraft developed by NAL
c. HTT-40 | iii. Advanced Light Helicopter, twin-engine
d. Hansa | iv. Basic turboprop trainer
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Dhruv – HAL's twin-engine Advanced Light Helicopter; LCH Prachand – HAL's light combat helicopter for high altitude (inducted 3 Oct 2022); HTT-40 – HAL basic turboprop trainer; Hansa – NAL light trainer aircraft.

s:
Match List-I (Aircraft) with List-II (Maker / where built):
List-I | List-II
a. C-130J Super Hercules | i. HAL Kanpur (licence)
b. C-17 Globemaster III | ii. Boeing, USA
c. Dornier Do-228 | iii. Lockheed Martin, USA
d. Su-30MKI | iv. HAL Nashik (licence)
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: C-130J – Lockheed Martin (USA); C-17 Globemaster III – Boeing (USA); Dornier Do-228 – German design licence-built by HAL Kanpur; Su-30MKI – Russian (Sukhoi) design licence-built by HAL Nashik.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. INS Vikrant (IAC-1), India's first indigenous aircraft carrier, was built by Cochin Shipyard.
2. INS Vikrant (IAC-1) was commissioned by the Prime Minister on 2 September 2023.
3. With INS Arihant, India became the sixth country with an armed nuclear submarine (SSBN).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct (Cochin Shipyard built IAC-1; Arihant made India the 6th SSBN nation, Aug 2016). 2 is wrong: Vikrant was commissioned on 2 September 2022, not 2023.

s:
Consider the following statements about India's submarines:
1. The Kalvari-class Scorpene submarines are built under Project 75.
2. INS Sindhurakshak, which sank after a fire in Mumbai in 2013, was a French Scorpene boat.
3. Vaghsheer is the last boat of Project 75.
4. For Project-75(I), Navantia of Spain signed a teaming agreement with Mazagon Dock in July 2023.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct (Kalvari class = P-75 Scorpenes by MDL; Vaghsheer is the last). 2 is wrong: Sindhurakshak was a Russian Kilo-class boat. 4 is wrong: Navantia's P-75(I) teaming partner (July 2023) is L&T.

s:
Consider the following statements about Project 17A:
1. It consists of seven Nilgiri-class stealth frigates.
2. The ships are being built by Mazagon Dock and Cochin Shipyard.
3. The ships carry the MF-STAR AESA radar.
4. Mahendragiri, the seventh ship, joined the Western Fleet in July 2026.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct (7 Nilgiri-class stealth frigates with MF-STAR and BrahMos). 2 is wrong: they are built by MDL and GRSE, not Cochin Shipyard. 4 is wrong: Mahendragiri joined the Eastern Fleet on 18 July 2026.

s:
Match List-I (Ship) with List-II (Fact):
List-I | List-II
a. Surat | i. Built at Yantar shipyard, Russia (2025)
b. Tavasya | ii. Stealth frigate of the P-1135.6 follow-on project, launched at Goa Shipyard
c. INS Tamal | iii. P17A frigate commissioned at Visakhapatnam in April 2026
d. Taragiri | iv. Fourth and last destroyer of Project 15B
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Surat – last P15B destroyer (2025); Tavasya – P-1135.6 follow-on stealth frigate, Goa Shipyard (March 2025); INS Tamal – built at Yantar, Russia; Taragiri – P17A frigate commissioned at Visakhapatnam (April 2026).

s:
Match List-I (Explosive) with List-II (Other name):
List-I | List-II
a. HMX | i. Picric acid
b. CL-20 | ii. HNIW
c. Trinitrophenol (TNP) | iii. Hexogen
d. RDX | iv. Octogen
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: HMX – Octogen (High Melting Explosive); CL-20 – HNIW (most powerful non-nuclear explosive, HEMRL Pune); TNP – picric acid; RDX – cyclonite / hexogen / T-4.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The chemical formula of TNT is C₇H₅N₃O₆.
2. RDX is chemically trinitrophenol.
3. LLM-105 is an insensitive high explosive.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: RDX is cyclotrimethylenetrinitramine, (O₂NNCH₂)₃; trinitrophenol is picric acid (TNP).

s:
Consider the following statements about explosives:
1. Gun cotton is cellulose nitrate, made by treating cotton or wood fibre with nitric and sulphuric acids.
2. Gun cotton is also used in printing inks, leather finishing and celluloid.
3. Amatol is a mixture of TNT and potassium nitrate.
4. Cordite, a propellant, contains nitroglycerine and nitrocellulose.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: 1, 2 and 4 are correct. 3 is wrong: Amatol is TNT + ammonium nitrate (it has no nitroglycerine).

s:
Consider the following statements about the Doppler effect:
1. A sound source moving towards a listener sounds higher in pitch.
2. A red shift in the light of a star shows that the star is approaching the Earth.
3. It is used in medical ultrasound to measure blood-flow velocity.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: a red shift (lower frequency) means the star is moving away – the basis of the expanding-universe idea (Hubble).

s:
Match List-I (Radar) with List-II (Role):
List-I | List-II
a. Arudhra | i. IAF medium-power 4D surveillance radar
b. Ashwini | ii. Low-level lightweight AESA radar against cruise missiles and drones
c. INDRA | iii. Low-level surveillance (Indian Doppler Radar)
d. Synthetic Aperture Radar | iv. Imaging at night and through clouds
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Arudhra – IAF medium-power 4D surveillance radar; Ashwini – low-level lightweight AESA radar (cruise missiles, drones); INDRA – low-level surveillance; SAR – imaging at night and through clouds.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Over-the-horizon radar bounces HF waves off the ionosphere.
2. The Uttam AESA radar of the Tejas Mk-1A was developed by DLRL.
3. An AESA radar steers its beam electronically, with a T/R module on every element.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: Uttam, the solid-state AESA fire-control radar of the Tejas Mk-1A, is from LRDE, not DLRL.

s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): The Swathi radar made by BEL is used to locate enemy guns, mortars and rockets.
Reason (R): India has exported the Swathi radar to Armenia.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true: Swathi is BEL's weapon-locating radar and it has been exported to Armenia. But the export does not explain what the radar does, so R is not the explanation of A.

s:
Consider the following statements about AWACS and AEW&C systems:
1. India's Netra AEW&C is mounted on the Embraer EMB-145.
2. Netra was built by DRDO-CABS, Bengaluru.
3. AWACS is mounted on a smaller jet than Netra and offers only limited control.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: AWACS (e.g., Il-76 Phalcon) is the larger aircraft with longer range and full battle management; Netra is the smaller jet with early warning and limited control.

s:
Match List-I (Shipyard) with List-II (Fact):
List-I | List-II
a. Hindustan Shipyard | i. Located at Vasco da Gama
b. GRSE | ii. Under the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
c. Cochin Shipyard | iii. Built Jala Usha (1948)
d. Goa Shipyard | iv. First Indian yard to export a warship (Mauritius, 2014)
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Hindustan Shipyard (Visakhapatnam) built Jala Usha in 1948; GRSE (Kolkata) was the first Indian yard to export a warship (Mauritius, 2014); Cochin Shipyard is under the Ministry of Ports, Shipping & Waterways; Goa Shipyard is at Vasco da Gama.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. India's first indigenous hydrogen fuel cell ferry was flagged off by the Prime Minister from Varanasi.
2. The hydrogen ferry was built by Cochin Shipyard under the Harit Nauka initiative.
3. Hindustan Shipyard was set up in 1941 by Scindia Steam Navigation Company.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is wrong: the PM flagged the ferry off virtually from Thoothukudi (28 Feb 2024); Varanasi is where it is meant to operate.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Indian Coast Guard:
1. It was set up in 1977.
2. Its coastal radar chain set up after 26/11 has 84 radar stations.
3. Its eight Adamya-class fast patrol vessels are being built by GRSE.
4. The H-561 is India's first indigenous hovercraft (air cushion vehicle).
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: 1, 2 and 4 are correct. 3 is wrong: the eight Adamya-class fast patrol vessels are built by Goa Shipyard, not GRSE.

s:
Match List-I (System) with List-II (Developer):
List-I | List-II
a. Zorawar light tank | i. BEL with the Army
b. ATAGS | ii. NIBE with Israel
c. Suryastra | iii. DRDO's ARDE
d. Akashteer | iv. DRDO with L&T
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Zorawar – DRDO with L&T; ATAGS (155 mm/52-cal towed gun) – DRDO ARDE; Suryastra (300 km universal rocket launcher) – NIBE with Israel; Akashteer (air-defence control network) – BEL with the Army.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Arjun main battle tank was developed by DRDO's CVRDE, Avadi.
2. The Pinaka LRGR-120 had its maiden test at Pokhran in December 2025.
3. The Russian T-90S tank is licence-built at the Heavy Vehicles Factory, Avadi.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: the Pinaka LRGR-120 (120 km) had its maiden test at ITR Chandipur on 29 Dec 2025, not Pokhran.

s:
Consider the following statements about Indian UAVs:
1. Lakshya is a pilotless target drone developed by DRDO-ADE.
2. Ghatak is a stealth flying-wing UCAV.
3. Netra is a mini UAV developed by HAL with Boeing.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: Netra is a DRDO mini UAV made with ideaForge – not a HAL-Boeing product.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. A new submarine base of the Eastern Naval Command is coming up at Rambilli.
2. INS Dega at Visakhapatnam is a naval air station.
3. A DRDO test range is located near Kurnool in Andhra Pradesh.
4. The Information Fusion Centre – Indian Ocean Region (IFC-IOR) was set up by the Navy at Visakhapatnam in 2018.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: 1, 2 and 3 are correct. 4 is wrong: the IFC-IOR was set up by the Navy at Gurugram in 2018.

s:
Match List-I (System) with List-II (Type):
List-I | List-II
a. Varunastra | i. Integrated submarine sonar
b. TAL | ii. Anti-torpedo decoy
c. Maareech | iii. Ship-launched heavyweight anti-submarine torpedo
d. USHUS | iv. Lightweight torpedo launched from helicopters and the P-8I
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Varunastra – heavyweight ship-launched anti-submarine torpedo (NSTL); TAL – lightweight torpedo from MH-60R, Dhruv and P-8I; Maareech – anti-torpedo decoy; USHUS – integrated submarine sonar.

s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): An Air Independent Propulsion (AIP) system lets a diesel-electric submarine stay submerged longer without snorkelling.
Reason (R): DRDO's AIP system is a Russian design meant for nuclear submarines.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: A is true. R is false: DRDO's AIP is an indigenous NMRL fuel-cell system for diesel-electric (not nuclear) boats.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. INS Astradharini, India's first indigenous torpedo launch and recovery vessel, was commissioned at Kochi in 2015.
2. ERASR, the anti-submarine rocket tried from INS Kavaratti, was developed by ARDE, Pune.
3. SMART stands for Supersonic Missile Assisted Release of Torpedo.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is wrong: INS Astradharini was commissioned on 6 Oct 2015 at Visakhapatnam, not Kochi.

s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): Akash Tarang, approved by the DAC in July 2026, is a soft-kill anti-drone system.
Reason (R): It jams the control signals of hostile drones instead of destroying them physically.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true and R explains A: Akash Tarang is an electronic-warfare system – jamming control signals is exactly what makes it 'soft kill'.

s:
Match List-I (Product / work) with List-II (DRDO lab):
List-I | List-II
a. Kanchan armour | i. DMRL, Hyderabad
b. 2-DG anti-COVID drug | ii. INMAS with Dr Reddy's
c. Bukhari heater and Cognobar | iii. DIPAS
d. High-altitude agriculture and herbal products | iv. DIHAR, Leh
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Kanchan armour (Arjun) – DMRL Hyderabad; 2-DG – INMAS with Dr Reddy's (2021); Bukhari heater and Cognobar – DIPAS; high-altitude agriculture and herbal products – DIHAR, Leh.

s:
Match List-I (Event) with List-II (Fact):
List-I | List-II
a. DefExpo 2018 | i. Held in 1999
b. DefExpo 2020 | ii. Lucknow; theme 'India: The Emerging Defence Manufacturing Hub'
c. DefExpo 2022 | iii. 12th edition, Gandhinagar (Gujarat)
d. First DefExpo | iv. Held near Chennai, Tamil Nadu
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: DefExpo 2018 – near Chennai, Tamil Nadu (iDEX launched there); DefExpo 2020 – Lucknow, theme 'India: The Emerging Defence Manufacturing Hub'; DefExpo 2022 – 12th edition, Gandhinagar ('Path to Pride'); the first DefExpo was in 1999.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. RAKSHA (Sep 2026) is a five-year roadmap for global defence partnerships.
2. Samudra Laksamana is a naval exercise between India and Malaysia.
3. The 3rd edition of Samudra Laksamana (28 Feb – 2 Mar 2024) was held off Visakhapatnam.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is wrong: RAKSHA is a 10-year roadmap for global defence partnerships.

s:
Consider the following statements about iDEX:
1. iDEX (Innovations for Defence Excellence) was launched by the Prime Minister in April 2018.
2. The Defence Innovation Organisation, which runs iDEX, was set up by DRDO.
3. ADITI under iDEX funds deep-tech areas such as AI, quantum technologies, hypersonics and directed energy.
4. Under the Defence India Startup Challenge, the problem statements are set by the Services.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: 1, 3 and 4 are correct. 2 is wrong: DIO is a not-for-profit (Sec. 8) company set up by HAL and BEL, not DRDO.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Technology Development Fund (TDF) of the Ministry of Defence is executed by DRDO.
2. TDF grants are capped at Rs 25 crore per project.
3. Bellatrix Aerospace's TDF-funded green propulsion thruster was proved in orbit on PSLV-C58.
4. SRIJAN is an indigenisation portal.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1, 3 and 4 are correct. 2 is wrong: TDF grants go up to Rs 50 crore per project.

s:
Match List-I (Company) with List-II (Product):
List-I | List-II
a. Bharat Dynamics Ltd | i. Su-30MKI licence-built at Nashik
b. Bharat Electronics Ltd | ii. Guided missiles such as Akash and Astra
c. BEML | iii. Earth movers
d. HAL | iv. Swathi weapon-locating radar
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: BDL (Hyderabad, 1970) – guided missiles; BEL – defence electronics such as the Swathi WLR; BEML – earth movers; HAL – aircraft and helicopters, incl. the Su-30MKI at Nashik and Dhruv.

s:
Match List-I (Partnership / project) with List-II (Outcome):
List-I | List-II
a. India–South Korea roadmap (2020) | i. Marine gas turbine 'Samudra' from the Kaveri engine
b. Bharat Forge (May 2026) | ii. Army Research Cell at IIT Madras
c. GTRE | iii. K9 Vajra-T self-propelled gun
d. Agnishodh | iv. First private marine gas turbine MRO at Visakhapatnam
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: India–South Korea – K9 Vajra-T; Bharat Forge – first private marine gas turbine MRO, Visakhapatnam; GTRE – 'Samudra' marine gas turbine from Kaveri; Agnishodh – Army Research Cell at IIT Madras (4 Aug 2025).

s:
Consider the following statements about defence procurement reforms:
1. In May 2001 the defence sector was opened to Indian private participation with FDI up to 26%.
2. The Buy (Indian-IDDM) category was first added in DAP 2020.
3. The Strategic Partnership model was added in 2017.
4. DAP 2020 dropped offsets in government-to-government and single-vendor deals.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: 1, 3 and 4 are correct. 2 is wrong: Buy (Indian-IDDM) was first added in DPP 2016; DAP 2020 made it the top priority.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. In 2021 the 41 factories of the Ordnance Factory Board were regrouped into seven DPSUs.
2. Gliders India is one of the DPSUs formed from the OFB.
3. The Ministry of Defence declared 2025 the 'Year of Reforms'.
4. The Defence Procurement Manual 2025 governs capital procurement.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1, 2 and 3 are correct. 4 is wrong: DPM 2025 (23 Oct 2025) governs revenue procurement of about Rs 1 lakh crore; capital buys come under DAP 2020.

s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): Under DAP 2020, Buy (Indian-IDDM) is the most preferred procurement category.
Reason (R): DAP 2020 has five buy categories.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true: Buy (Indian-IDDM) is priority 1 of the five DAP 2020 categories. But the number of categories does not explain why IDDM is preferred (the indigenous-design push does), so R is not the explanation of A.

s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): FDI in defence above 74% is permitted through the automatic route.
Reason (R): FDI in defence up to 74% is permitted through the automatic route.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: A is false: FDI above 74% (up to 100%) needs the government route. R is true: up to 74% is automatic.

s:
Consider the following statements about India's defence production and exports:
1. Defence production reached a record Rs 1.78 lakh crore in FY 2025-26.
2. Defence exports rose from Rs 686 crore in 2013-14 to Rs 23,622 crore in 2024-25.
3. Indonesia is a buyer of the BrahMos missile and the Philippines of the Astra missile.
4. India still imports jet engines and defence chips.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1, 2 and 4 are correct. 3 is wrong: the pairs are reversed – the Philippines bought BrahMos and Indonesia is associated with Astra.

s:
Consider the following statements about the defence industrial corridors:
1. The two corridors are in Uttar Pradesh and Tamil Nadu.
2. The Uttar Pradesh corridor has five nodes.
3. The BrahMos unit of the Uttar Pradesh corridor is at Lucknow.
4. Hosur is a node of the Tamil Nadu corridor.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1, 3 and 4 are correct. 2 is wrong: the UP corridor has six nodes (Agra, Aligarh, Chitrakoot, Jhansi, Kanpur, Lucknow); it is the Tamil Nadu corridor that has five.

s:
Match List-I (Andhra Pradesh unit) with List-II (Purpose):
List-I | List-II
a. BEL Palasamudram | i. Eastern Naval Command submarine base
b. BEL Machilipatnam | ii. Torpedoes, mines and AUVs
c. Rambilli | iii. Opto-electronics and night vision
d. NSTL, Visakhapatnam | iv. Missile and radar systems integration
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: BEL Palasamudram (Sri Sathya Sai district) – missile and radar systems integration; BEL Machilipatnam – opto-electronics / night vision; Rambilli (Anakapalli) – new submarine base of the Eastern Naval Command; NSTL – DRDO naval weapons lab (Varunastra, mines, AUVs).

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Energy intensity is the energy used per unit of GDP.
2. A rising energy intensity shows that growth is decoupling from energy use.
3. Peak demand is the highest power drawn on the grid in a 15-minute interval.
4. An 'energy crisis' refers to the danger that fossil fuels such as coal and petroleum may run out.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1, 3 and 4 are correct. 2 is wrong: it is a falling energy intensity that shows growth decoupling from energy use.

s:
Consider the following statements about India's energy mix:
1. Coal supplies about 55% of India's energy mix and over 74% of its power generation.
2. After fossil fuels, wind is the second source of India's energy supply.
3. The non-fossil share of installed power capacity rose from 32% in 2014 to 51% in 2025.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: after fossil fuels the second source of supply is solar (UPPSC 2021), not wind.

s:
Consider the following statements about India's per-capita energy use:
1. Per-capita electricity consumption rose from 957 kWh in FY14 to about 1,460 kWh in FY25.
2. India's per-capita electricity consumption is about one-half of China's.
3. India's per-capita energy consumption is about one-third of the world average.
4. Per-capita energy use shows a large urban-rural gap.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1, 3 and 4 are correct. 2 is wrong: India's per-capita electricity use is about one-fifth of China's (and one-ninth of the USA's).

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Industry uses about 50% of India's electricity.
2. Industry is projected to remain the largest energy consumer in India by 2040.
3. Cooking energy demand in India is projected to rise sharply by 2040.
4. The Saubhagya scheme connected about 26 million households.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: 1, 2 and 4 are correct. 3 is wrong: cooking energy demand is projected to fall by 2040.

s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): India's peak electricity demand rose by about 37%, from 183 GW in December 2020 to over 250 GW in April 2026.
Reason (R): Electric vehicles, farm pumps, appliances, cooling and data centres are driving up peak demand.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true and R explains A: these new loads are the drivers of the rising peak.

s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): The evening peak has become central to India's storage push.
Reason (R): On 25 April 2026 India's electricity deficit occurred mainly during solar hours.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: A is true. R is false: on 25 April 2026 there was no shortage in solar hours; the ~2% deficit was in non-solar (evening, 6–11 p.m.) hours – which is why storage matters.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. India's record peak demand of 270.8 GW (May 2026) was about 90 GW above 2019.
2. Delhi has responded to the evening peak with Time-of-Day tariffs and smart meters.
3. AT&C losses fell from 22.62% in FY14 to about 10.04% in FY25.
4. Poor storage and slow transmission cause regional imbalances in renewable power.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1, 2 and 4 are correct. 3 is wrong: AT&C losses fell to 15.04% in FY25.

s:
Match List-I (Report) with List-II (Publisher):
List-I | List-II
a. Energy Statistics | i. NITI Aayog
b. India Energy Security Scenarios 2047 | ii. International Energy Agency
c. World Energy Outlook | iii. MoEFCC
d. India Cooling Action Plan | iv. National Statistics Office (MoSPI)
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Energy Statistics – CSO, now NSO (MoSPI); IESS 2047 – NITI Aayog; World Energy Outlook – IEA; India Cooling Action Plan (2019) – MoEFCC.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. NITI Aayog's IESS expects India's energy demand to rise 2.7–3.2 times between 2012 and 2040.
2. According to the IEA's World Energy Outlook 2022, India's coal generation and oil imports peak around 2040.
3. The CEA's National Generation Adequacy Plan projects a peak demand of 459 GW by 2035-36.
4. IESS expects electricity demand to rise 4.5-fold between 2012 and 2040.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1, 3 and 4 are correct. 2 is wrong: WEO 2022 sees India's coal generation and oil imports peaking around 2030.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. About 88% of India's crude oil is imported.
2. About 50% of India's natural gas (LNG) need is met by imports.
3. During the 2026 gas crisis, the Strait of Malacca was identified as the main risk to India's LPG supplies.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: the risk identified was the Strait of Hormuz.

s:
Match List-I (Commitment / status) with List-II (Emission-intensity cut versus 2005):
List-I | List-II
a. First NDC (2015) | i. 47% by 2035
b. Updated NDC (Aug 2022) | ii. 36%
c. New NDC for 2031–35 | iii. 33–35% by 2030
d. Cut already achieved | iv. 45% by 2030
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: First NDC – 33–35% by 2030; updated NDC (2022) – 45% by 2030; new NDC 2031–35 – 47% by 2035; emission intensity is already 36% below 2005.

x: 1, 2 and 4 are correct. 3 is wrong: the draft policy targets 100 GW of pumped storage by 2047.

3. About 5,588 MW of new thermal capacity is sought, of which APERC cleared the first 1,600 MW.

x: 2, 3 and 4 are correct. 1 is wrong: the central VGF project with NHPC is 500 MW / 1,000 MWh.

2. India's LPG supply depends mainly on the stocks of oil marketing companies.
3. India is the second-largest oil consumer in the world.
4. OPEC's share of India's crude imports fell below 50% by August 2025.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1, 2 and 4 are correct. 3 is wrong: India is the third-largest oil consumer (and third-largest energy consumer).

Consider the following statements about the 2026 Hormuz shock:
1. The Strait of Hormuz lies between Iran and Oman.
2. About one-third of world crude-oil trade passes through it.
3. After its closure India proposed a 41 MT strategic fuel system.
4. India's crude-oil import bill in FY 2024-25 was $13.7 billion.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: 1, 2 and 3 are correct. 4 is wrong: the FY 2024-25 crude import bill was $137.0 billion; $13.7 billion was the bill for July 2026 alone.

s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): A rise in international oil prices widens India's trade deficit.
Reason (R): Crude-oil imports are the biggest driver of India's trade deficit and current account deficit.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true and R explains A: because crude imports dominate the import bill, costlier oil directly widens the trade deficit (and feeds inflation).

Consider the following statements about the Methanol Economy:
1. Di-Methyl Ether (DME) is formed from two methanol molecules by removing one water molecule.
2. DME can replace propane in LPG.
3. The M15 blend has 15% methanol in diesel.
4. Blending 20% DME in LPG can save about Rs 6,000 crore a year.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: 1, 2 and 4 are correct. 3 is wrong: M15 is 15% methanol in petrol, expected to cut petrol/crude imports by at least 15%.

2. The Compressed Biogas Obligation in city gas distribution is 5% of CNG/PNG from FY 2025-26.
3. The Compressed Biogas Obligation mainly aims to replace LNG imports.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: the obligation is 1% in FY 2025-26, rising to 3%, 4% and 5% only from 2028-29.

2. India has the world's third-largest coal reserves.
3. Of India's 26 sedimentary basins, only 7 are producing.
4. The large low-grade uranium deposit at Tummalapalle is in YSR Kadapa district.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: 1, 3 and 4 are correct. 2 is wrong: India has the world's fifth-largest coal reserves (it is the second-largest producer).

2. DISCOMs and open-access or captive users must buy a prescribed share of renewable power.
3. A 'prosumer' is a consumer who also produces or stores power and sells the surplus to the grid.
4. The Tariff Policy of 2006 was revised in 2016.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: 2, 3 and 4 are correct. 1 is wrong: under the Electricity Act 2003, RPOs are fixed by the State Electricity Regulatory Commissions (SERCs).

2. They aim to meet 60% of the energy requirement from renewables by 2030.
3. They aim to cut projected cumulative emissions by 1 billion tonnes by 2030.
4. They were announced at COP26, Glasgow.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1, 3 and 4 are correct. 2 is wrong: the target is 50% (not 60%) of energy requirement from renewables by 2030.

2. India's updated NDC (2022) targets 50% non-fossil installed capacity by 2030.
3. India's new NDC (2031–35) aims to cut the emissions intensity of GDP by 47% by 2035.
4. India's goal of energy independence is linked to the year 2047.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 2, 3 and 4 are correct. 1 is wrong: the LT-LEDS was submitted at COP27 (2022), not COP26.

4. It recommended market-determined pricing and subsidies targeted to the poor.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: 1, 2 and 4 are correct. 3 is wrong: its horizon was 2031-32, not 2047.

Consider the following statements about the National Clean Energy Fund:
1. It was financed by a clean energy cess on coal.
2. The cess, introduced at Rs 50 per tonne in 2010-11, rose to Rs 400 per tonne by 2016-17.

x: All three are correct: the NCEF was funded by the clean energy cess on coal (Budget 2010-11, Rs 50 → Rs 400/tonne by 2016-17), which was folded into the GST Compensation Cess in 2017.
